neighbours.label: Where governmental power is placed: the words around 'power/authority is vested in, lodged in, concentrated in, shifted to' a body of state, vs the same verbs describing non-political things
fire: Under the new charter, executive power is vested in an elected president.
In a federal system, authority is divided between the capital and the states.
After the coup, all power was concentrated in the hands of the army.
The treaty transferred sovereign authority from the crown to the parliament.
In that kingdom, judicial power rests with a council of elders.
The reform moved real power away from the king and toward the assembly.
Constitutionally, the power to declare war lies with the legislature.
Over the century, political power drifted from the nobles to the merchants.
quiet: Under the new lease, the parking space is assigned to an upstairs tenant.
In a large kitchen, work is divided between the chefs and the porters.
After the storm, all the leaves were piled in the corner of the yard.
The truck transferred the furniture from the old house to the new one.
In that orchard, the oldest tree rests beside a small stone wall.
The wind moved the boat away from the dock and toward the island.
In the recipe, the power of the oven should be set to medium.
Over the summer, the sand drifted from the beach onto the road.

predictions: Fire items 0.3-0.9 on the verb or article after political 'power'; near misses under 0.1.
notes: Card: ' the', ' is', ' been', ' السلطة', '的' in constitutional prose ('sovereign power is lodged in', 'legislative power is vested in', 'power shifting from the monarch').
